content: WBP11, also known as WW domain binding protein 11, is alternatively referred to as Npw38-binding protein (NpwBP), splicing factor that interacts with PQBP-1 and PP1 (SIPP1), and SH3 domain binding protein, 70 kDa (SNP70). Functional studies indicate that WBP11 is involved in DNA/RNA transcriptional or post-transcriptional processes associated with cell division. Within interphase cells, WBP11 is localized in the nucleus but is absent from the nucleoli. During cell division, however, it redistributes throughout the cytoplasm. Immunoelectron microscopy experiments suggest that this relocation, from a perinuclear to a cytoplasmic distribution, coincides with the onset of mitosis. Additional studies have demonstrated that WBP11 is a component of the spliceosome and that fragments of WBP11 can inhibit pre-mRNA splicing catalysis. WBP11 is a polypeptide that interacts with other WW domain-containing proteins, such as the nuclear protein Npw38, through two proline-rich regions. It associates with Npw38 in the nucleus and also binds to Poly(rG) and G-rich single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). The 70 kDa protein has been shown to interact with SH3 (Src homology domain 3) domains. The C-terminal proline-rich sequences of SNP70/NpwBP/WBP11, which bind to the WW domain of Npw38, conform to both classic type I and type II SH3 binding sequences, justifying its designation as SNP70. WBP11 exhibits strong binding to the tandem SH3 domains of p47phox and the N-terminal SH3 domain of p47phox, while showing weaker interactions with the SH3 domains of c-src and p85α. Furthermore, WBP11 has been shown to interact with protein phosphatase 1 (PP1), earning it the name SIPP1. It exerts an inhibitory effect on PP1, with its inhibitory potency increasing upon phosphorylation by protein kinase CK1. The interaction between WBP11 and PP1 involves an RVXF (Arg-Val-Xaa-Phe) motif, which serves as a PP1-binding sequence in most PP1 interactors.
